web.welcome.title: Save data sync
web.welcome.lede: Download your save anywhere and play.
web.welcome.sub: DaeMoon backs up and syncs saves for the 3DS, the Switch and nds-bootstrap. Every version is kept, and nothing is ever merged behind your back.
web.welcome.warn_head: Never sync while a game is running.
web.welcome.warn: A running game holds its save open, so writing to it corrupts what the game saves next and reading it returns something stale. Sync before you start a game or after you close it. This is the one thing no amount of care here can protect you from.
web.welcome.f1.v: Nothing is replaced. An upload adds a version and the ones before it stay downloadable, so choosing wrong is something you can undo tomorrow.
web.welcome.f2.v: When two consoles disagree, you pick a side and both sides survive. A restore writes a backup to the card first, every time, with no way to switch that off.
web.welcome.f3.v: A console reaches your server over Wi-Fi, wherever either of them happens to be. Leave a save on one console and the next one to sync picks it up.
web.welcome.dl_3ds_note: A CIA, installed with FBI. It has to be a CIA: a 3dsx cannot reach another title's save archive.
web.welcome.qr.head: Scan this with the console
web.welcome.qr.how: In FBI: Remote Install, then Scan QR Code. The console downloads the current build and installs it, so nothing has to reach the SD card by hand.
web.welcome.dl_nx_note: An NRO, for Atmosphere. Early: nothing in it has been checked on real hardware yet.
web.welcome.dl_server_note: The binary behind this page, for Linux, macOS and Windows, or as a container image.
web.welcome.naming: Every file is named after the commit it was built from, so a build sitting on an SD card months later can still say which one it is. Check it against SHA256SUMS before installing something that writes to save data.
web.welcome.kicker: Save data sync for 3DS, Switch and nds-bootstrap
web.welcome.gate.head: What a sync compares
web.welcome.gate.up: The console is ahead, so it uploads.
web.welcome.gate.clash: Both moved on. You choose, and both survive.
web.welcome.gate.note: No clock appears anywhere on this card. Freshness is the version the server issued, because a console clock is user settable.
web.welcome.order.head: The order a sync happens in
web.welcome.s1.v: The save is read into a zip with a manifest beside it, and the payload is hashed on the way in.
web.welcome.s2.v: The version the console started from against the server's latest. Matching numbers accept, differing ones are a conflict.
web.welcome.s3.v: A package reaches the SD card before one byte is written to a save archive. There is no switch that turns this off.
web.welcome.s4.v: The archive is committed and the digest checked. Skip that and the console keeps nothing, and the game is what finds out.
web.welcome.no2: Merge two saves. You pick a side, and the side you did not pick stays downloadable afterwards.
web.welcome.no3: Trust a clock. Freshness comes from the version the server issued and from nothing else.
web.welcome.no4: Restore without backing up first. The copy is on the card before anything is overwritten, every time.
welcome.title: Welcome
welcome.what: DaeMoon copies this console's saves to a server you run, and brings them back. The same save on two consoles, without moving the card.
welcome.safe: A local backup is always made before anything is restored, and a conflict is never merged for you: both versions are kept and you choose.
welcome.when: Sync before you start a game or after you quit it, never while one is running. A game holds its save open, and writing to it then breaks it.
welcome.connect_how: Sign in to the panel in a browser and press Add a console. It shows a code.
welcome.opt_qr_hint: Nothing to type. The code carries the server address with it, so this console needs no address set first.
welcome.opt_code: Type the address and the code
welcome.opt_code_hint: For when the camera cannot read a screen. Two things to type on the keyboard, and it always works.
welcome.opt_later_hint: Backing up to the SD card works without a server. Settings has this screen's choices whenever you want them.
welcome.ready: This console is connected. Back one save up first and restore it, on a game you are not attached to, before trusting it with one you are.
welcome.later: Nothing is connected, and backing up to the SD card works anyway. Settings has the server and the pairing rows when you want them.

batch.sync_hint: Covers both libraries, the installed titles and the DS saves. Uploads what only this console changed and downloads what only the server changed. What happens when both changed is the next question.

batch.policy_local_hint: This console's save goes on top as a new version. The server keeps everything it already had, so the other side is still there to go back to.
batch.policy_server_hint: The server's save is written over this console's. Each one is backed up to the SD card first, so what is replaced is still on the card.
